title: What to Do When Someone Dies in Lesotho: 5-Step Official Checklist
titleEn: What to Do When Someone Dies in Lesotho: 5-Step Official Checklist
cardSummary: Official 5-step bereavement checklist for Lesotho: medical death certification, civil death registration, funeral and repatriation permits, survivor benefits, and estate succession.
introHtml: Handling a death in Lesotho requires securing a medical cause-of-death certificate for civil registration, reporting the estate to the Master of the High Court under the unified 2024 inheritance statute, claiming public or occupational pension death benefits within statutory deadlines, and using Hague Apostilles for cross-border documents. Because several Lesotho central government portals (including Ministry of Health and Foreign Affairs domains and the revenue portal) time out or fail TLS validation from external networks, this guide relies on verified Ministry of Home Affairs NICR pages, PODCPF, Parliament of Lesotho reports, StarLight Oasis of Hope Hospice, Partners In Health Lesotho, HCCH authority listings, and LesLII statutes.

steps.title: Immediate Medical Confirmation and Death Registration
steps.html:
• Obtain a medical certificate giving the cause of death from the attending physician; for a hospital death, a hospital doctor places the certificate in a sealed envelope addressed to National Identity and Civil Registration (NICR) [1].
  • For a death outside a hospital setting, obtain local confirmation from the village chief or local authority alongside witness statements required for civil registration [2][6].
  • Submit the medical certificate, identity particulars of the deceased, and informant details to the Ministry of Home Affairs (NICR) to register the death and collect the official Death Certificate [1][2][3].

steps.title: Estate Reporting and Probate under the 2024 Act
steps.html:
• Lesotho's Administration of Estates and Inheritance Act, 2024 (Act No. 2 of 2024, operational from 2 April 2024) repealed and replaced the 1935 Administration of Estates Proclamation and customary succession dualism, bringing all civil and customary estates under the unified supervision of the Master of the High Court [6][7].
  • Report the death notice, deposit any original will, and submit required inventory forms to the Master of the High Court to obtain Letters of Administration (or apply through simplified chief-certified documentation for qualifying small estates up to M145,000) [6][7].

steps.title: Pension, Survivor, and Funeral Benefit Claims
steps.html:
• Notify the Public Officers' Defined Contribution Pension Fund (PODCPF) within 6 months of death for pre-retirement death-in-service or pensioner death claims; PODCPF provides accumulated fund credit plus risk cover equal to twice annual salary on pre-retirement death [4][5].
  • Submit the PODCPF Death Claim forms along with certified copies of the Death Certificate, claimant national IDs, marriage certificate, birth certificates for minor dependants, and bank account confirmation [4][5].
  • Contact any private employer occupational funds or funeral insurers separately and seek bereavement support from StarLight Oasis of Hope Hospice or Partners In Health Lesotho where family support is needed [10][11].

steps.title: Financial Accounts, Property Transfers, and Revenue Clearance
steps.html:
• Present certified copies of the Death Certificate and Letters of Administration to Lesotho banks, insurance providers, and property registries before distributing or transferring estate assets [7].
  • Address outstanding personal income or estate tax clearances directly with local Revenue Services Lesotho offices, as its external portal faces TLS connection failures.

steps.title: Cross-Border Document Authentication (Hague Apostille)
steps.html:
• Lesotho is a Contracting Party to the HCCH 1961 Hague Apostille Convention (in force since 4 October 1966 by succession), so Lesotho Death Certificates and Letters of Administration used in other Convention states require an Apostille rather than consular legalization [8][12].
  • Request an Apostille from one of Lesotho's designated Competent Authorities recorded on HCCH: the Attorney-General, a Permanent Secretary of a Ministry or Department, the Registrar of the High Court, a Resident Magistrate, or a Magistrate of the First Class [8][9].

contacts.name: Public Officers' Defined Contribution Pension Fund (PODCPF)
contacts.note: 4th Floor Pension Fund House, Constitution Road, Maseru (Toll Free 80002778; WhatsApp +266 57702778); death claims within 6 months.

contacts.name: Registrar of the High Court
contacts.note: Designated Lesotho Apostille Competent Authority alongside the Attorney-General and Magistrates; Master of the High Court supervises estates under Act 2 of 2024.
